{{also|Appendix:Variations of "ant"}}
==English==

===Etymology===
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:-ant<ety:bor<fro:-ant>:inh<ang:-ende<id:participle>>>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|-ant}}, {{m|enm|-aunt}}, partly from {{der|en|fro|-ant}}, from {{der|en|la|-āns}}; and partly (in adjectival derivations) continuing {{inh|en|enm|-ant}}, a variant of {{m|enm|-and}}, {{m|enm|-end}}, from {{inh|en|ang|-ende|pos=present participle ending}}, see {{l|en|-and}}. {{false cognate|ms, id|-an}} (and so all its Austronesian cognates), and {{noncog|ar|ان||adjective forming suffix}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|ənt}}, {{IPA|en|/ənt/}}
* {{enPR|ĕnt|a=India}}, {{IPA|en|/enʈ/|[ë̞ɳʈ]}}
* {{hmp|en|-ent}}

===Suffix===
{{head|en|suffix|cat2=adjective-forming suffixes}}

# {{lb|en|nowadays|sciences|chiefly|medicine}} The [[agent]] noun derived from [[verb]].
#: ''[[serve]]'' → ''[[servant]]''
# An [[adjective]] corresponding to a [[noun]] in {{m|en|-ance}}, having the sense of "[[exhibit]]ing (the [[condition]] or [[process]] described by the noun)".
# An adjective derived from a verb, having the senses of: (a) "[[do]]ing (the verbal action)", and/or (b) "[[prone]]/[[tending]] to do (the verbal action)".
#: ''[[ascend]]'' → ''[[ascendant]]''
#: ''[[err]]'' → ''[[errant]]''
# {{alternative form of|en|-and}}.
#: ''blat'''ant''''', ''blic'''ant'''''; ''flipp'''ant''''', ''old-farr'''ant'''''

====Usage notes====
* Many words in ''-ant'' were not actually coined in English but rather borrowed directly from Old French, Middle French or Modern French.

====Derived terms====
{{suffixsee|en}}

====Related terms====
* {{l|en|-ance}}

===Anagrams===
* {{anagrams|en|a=ant|TNA|TAN|NTA|Nat|NAT|ATN|nat|Tan|tan|Nat.}}

{{cln|en|productive suffixes}}

==French==

===Etymology===
{{etymon|fr|id=-ing|:inh|fro:-ant<id:present participle>}}
{{inh+|fr|fro|-ant}}, from a merger of {{inh|fr|la|-āns|-antem}}, {{m|la|-ēns|-entem|pos=present participle suffix}} with {{inh|fr|la|-andus|-andum}}, {{m|la|-endus|-endum|pos=gerundive suffix}}.

Compare {{cog|it|-ante}}, {{m|it|-ando}}; {{cog|es|-ante}}, {{m|es|-ando}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{fr-IPA}}
* {{audio|fr|LL-Q150 (fra)-WikiLucas00--ant.wav|a=<<France>> (<<Lyon>>)}}
* {{audio|fr|LL-Q150 (fra)-Jérémy-Günther-Heinz Jähnick--ant.wav|a=<<France>> (<<Somain>>)}}

===Suffix===
{{fr-suffix}} {{q|invariable}}

# [[-ing]]; {{ng|suffix denoting the [[gerund]] and [[present participle]] of a verb}}
#: {{sufex|fr|jouer|t1=to play|jou'''ant'''|t2=playing}}
#: {{ux|fr|Mange'''ant''' du pain, j'ai trébuché sur une peau de banane.|Eat'''ing''' bread, I tripped over a banana peel.}}

===Suffix===
{{fr-adj}}

# {{l|en|-ant}}, [[-ing]]; {{ng|forms adjectives out of verbs}}
# {{lb|fr|rare}} {{ng|forms [[adjective]]s from words other than verbs}}
#: {{sufex|fr|abracadabra|abracadabrant}}

===Suffix===
{{fr-noun|m|f=+}}

# [[-er]]; {{ng|forms nouns out of verbs}}

====Usage notes====
* French present participles are used, chiefly in literary style, to replace [[relative clause]]s. In this case they are <u>not</u> inflected for number and gender: {{m|fr||une femme [[aimant]] ses enfants|t=a woman loving her children}}, equivalent to {{m|fr||une femme qui aime ses enfants|t=a woman who loves her children}}.
* Some present participles can also be used as actual adjectives. In this case they are inflected: {{m|fr||une femme aimante|t=a loving/caring woman}}. Such adjectival uses are [[lexicalise]]d, however, and (unlike in English) not all participles allow it.
* Unlike Spanish, English, Italian and Portuguese, it is grammatically incorrect to use the verb {{l|fr|être}} before a present participle for continuous tenses.

====Related terms====
* {{l|fr|-amment}}
* {{l|fr|-ance}}

{{ety|de|:inh|gmh:-ant<ety:bor<fro:-ant>>|tree=+}}
From {{inh|de|gmh|-ant}}, from {{der|de|la|-ans|-ans, -antis}}, in part through {{der|de|fro|-ant}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|de|/ant/|/ɑnt/}}
* {{audio|de|De--ant.ogg|a=<<Germany>> (<<Berlin>>)}}

===Suffix===
{{de-noun|m.weak|f=in}}

# {{senseid|de|agent noun}} {{n-g|Forms agent nouns, mostly from verbs of Romance or Latin origin.}}
#: {{suffixusex|de|liefern|t1=to supply|Lieferant|t2=supplier}}

====Usage notes====
* This ending is semi-{{glossary|productive}}, see e.g. {{m|de|Asylant}}, {{m|de|Antifant}}.
* This ending rarely also occurs in the neuter gender, see e.g. {{l|de|Antiozonant}}.

====Declension====
{{de-ndecl|m.weak}}

====Derived terms====
{{suffixsee|de}}
